correctness_confidence.basis: No material error found after reconstruction of both proofs and covariance, tail, normalization and concentration checks. Confidence is substantial but conditional on the cited external results, notably Han Theorem 1.5; this involved AI review is not independent or formal verification.

rigor.basis: The affine proof supplies both mesoscopic spectral-mass control and a least-singular-value cutoff, fixes the phase before N tends to infinity, and pays the actual perturbation energy. Polynomial size and sampling constants are correctly derived. Minor explicitness improvements remain.

novelty.basis: The unrestricted finite energy-constrained transfer and explicit polynomial witness guarantee are plausible new consequences relative to the primary sources inspected. The free determinant identity, operator capacity, subharmonicity, resolvent comparison and concentration are established tools; directed search does not establish worldwide priority.

significance.basis: Removes two substantive restrictions from the prior bridge and replaces extremely large constructive witnesses by a polynomial auxiliary-size guarantee in the positive-span class. General polynomial size, bit complexity, optimality of e and consequences beyond this optimization problem remain open.

reproducibility.basis: Exact source and PDF hashes, a frozen source snapshot, two own diagnostic programs and machine-readable results are preserved. These diagnostics inspect finite identities and constants; they do not reproduce the external infinite-dimensional proofs or provide independent model support.

summary: Favorable scientific recommendation for circulation as a working paper; no unresolved material objection was found in the exact eight-page PDF. The universal capacity sandwich and the separate Hermitian polynomial-size and sampling theorems withstand this audit. Ordinary quality score: 9.2/10. AIRR Millennium research-importance score: 6.0/10, not a conversion of the quality score or a probability of correctness. This is a shared-context OpenAI GPT-6 Astra AI assessment: this same reviewing context contributed to the affine transfer and phase-selection argument and exchanged technical feedback with the authoring context. It is involved_in_manuscript, not blind, isolated, human, formal, or an independent second vote. The judgment depends on the cited external theorems, especially the recent Han preprint, and does not certify priority, editorial acceptance or exceptional historical impact.
strengths: Universal comparison C/e <= F_infty <= C for arbitrary complex square tuples, including spaces without invertible scalar combinations or positive real span.
A finite invertible evaluation supplies an admissible perturbation; phase subharmonicity and normalization retain the target capacity constant without asserting convergence of the unperturbed model.
Affine determinant convergence explicitly controls the whole negative logarithmic tail using algebraicity, a shrinking-scale resolvent estimate and Han’s least-singular-value bound.
The Hermitian result gives every integer m >= max(2,ceil(4 d (a beta)^4 theta^-3)), normal auxiliary matrices, and a separately quantified Gaussian sampling guarantee.
weaknesses: The principal infinite-dimensional inputs are external; Han’s recent 50-page preprint was checked for exact applicability and read selectively, not re-proved in full.
No general polynomial auxiliary-size bound, efficient optimization of Q, finite-bit sampling analysis or sharpness of e is established.
Literature search was directed and limited. The exact combined statement was not found, but priority is unconfirmed and shifted free determinant theory has close prior work, including Kargin.
Reviewer involvement and reused shared context limit evidential independence. Numerical checks cannot rule out errors in the external theorems.
strong_novelty_candidates: The energy-normalized finite-dimensional realization of the Mai–Speicher capacity value to a universal factor e for arbitrary complex tuples, via an invertible in-space affine perturbation. Priority remains unconfirmed.

The covariance-dependent polynomial auxiliary-size estimate and explicit concentration guarantee for the Hermitian positive-span class. These are new consequences relative to sources checked, not new Gaussian comparison or concentration theorems.
